claims.claim: Language codes in symbol IDs use short forms defined authoritatively in the `LANG_CODES` constant in `src/types.ts`.
claims.rationale: Single source of truth; short codes save tokens across many ID occurrences.
claims.excerpt: The mapping is authoritative and lives as a single constant `LANG_CODES` in `src/types.ts`

claims.claim: Moving a symbol to a different file or renaming it changes its ID; incremental reindex rebinds claims as part of normal flow.
claims.rationale: These are semantic changes that legitimately produce new IDs; stale IDs in session context just return 'not found'.
claims.excerpt: **Moving a symbol to a different file changes its ID.**

claims.claim: Overloaded names in the same file collide under this ID scheme; the first declaration wins and subsequent overloads are not addressable via ID in MVP.
claims.rationale: Accepted limitation for MVP; disambiguators are deferred to a future major-version change.
claims.excerpt: **Overloaded names in the same file collide.** Two symbols with the same name at different lines in the same file produce the same ID.

claims.claim: Reference IDs use format `ref:<lang>:<path>:<line>` and do include line because a reference is a site, not an entity.
claims.rationale: A reference's identity is its location in a file, distinguishing it from symbol identity.
claims.excerpt: Reference IDs follow the same rule with `ref:` prefix and include line (because a reference *is* a site in a file, not an entity)

claims.claim: Symbol ID format must be `sym:<lang>:<path>:<name>` keyed to path + name, excluding line number from identity.
claims.rationale: Line numbers are volatile; including them would cascade ID churn on unrelated edits and break the reviewable-atlas property.
claims.excerpt: Symbol IDs follow a fixed format keyed to **path + name**, not line

claims.claim: Symbol IDs are stable public API consumed by Claude Code, third-party tooling, and persisted in atlas.json git history.
claims.rationale: IDs are committed artifacts read by team members and downstream tools; instability would cause noisy diffs and break cross-version compatibility.
claims.excerpt: They are no longer just within-session handles — they are tokens committed to the repo that every team member reads from.

claims.claim: The symbol ID format must not change in MVP or v0.x releases; a change requires a major version bump and explicit migration note.
claims.rationale: Third-party tools cannot defend against format drift with static types and rely on stability.
claims.excerpt: The format MUST NOT change in MVP or v0.x releases.

claims.claim: `LANG_CODES` is stable public API: adding entries is additive, but changing existing short codes is a breaking change requiring a major version bump.
claims.rationale: Short codes appear in committed symbol IDs; renaming them invalidates existing atlases.
claims.excerpt: changing existing short codes (e.g. renaming `ts` to `typescript`) is a breaking change requiring a major version bump

claims.claim: Consumers must read line numbers from the Symbol record's `line` field and never parse line from the ID.
claims.rationale: The ID does not contain line information; any code extracting line from ID is broken.
claims.excerpt: Any code that tries to extract line from ID is broken.

claims.claim: Line numbers are stored as supplementary metadata on the Symbol record, not embedded in the ID.
claims.rationale: Keeps line info available for debugging/navigation while preserving ID stability across line moves.
claims.excerpt: **Line numbers are supplementary metadata, not identity.**

claims.claim: Path normalization to forward-slash separators is required at every ingest boundary via the single `normalizePath()` utility.
claims.rationale: Ensures Windows and Linux developers produce byte-identical IDs; bypassing it creates silent duplicate-symbol bifurcation.
claims.excerpt: **Path normalization is required at ingest.** All paths in symbol IDs ... use forward-slash separators, even on Windows.

claims.claim: `normalizePath()` must be called at every ingest boundary including LSP path reads, config parsing, atlas.json import, and ADR directory scans; code review should flag path-handling code that bypasses it.
claims.rationale: Forgetting it anywhere creates a bifurcation where IDs diverge between platforms.
claims.excerpt: It must be called at every ingest boundary: reading file paths from LSP, parsing config, importing atlas.json, scanning ADR directories.

claims.claim: `contextatlas list-extraction-sources` walks all three extraction streams (ADRs, source-symbol docstrings, filtered commit messages) and emits unified JSON manifest; zero API cost.
claims.rationale: Enables Phase A source-discovery substrate equivalence between Skill and CLI paths.
claims.excerpt: **ADDED** `contextatlas list-extraction-sources` CLI subcommand... Emits unified JSON manifest with per-source content/sha/path/symbol-metadata for Skill consumption via Read tool.

claims.claim: The extraction request body is exactly { model, max_tokens, messages } with no thinking field and no sampling params; all three streams send the same request, differing only in body content.
claims.rationale: Frozen extraction substrate preserved across v1.2 Phase 0/2 changes.
claims.excerpt: The extraction request body is still exactly `{ model, max_tokens, messages }`, with no `thinking` field and no sampling params

claims.claim: The extraction wrapper (createExtractionClient) and judge wrapper (createJudgeClient) are each the single retry layer; every messages.create is sent with { maxRetries: 0 } so the SDK never retries underneath the wrapper.
claims.rationale: Prevents stacked retries; wrapper owns retry policy (3 retries, 1000 ms base, 30 000 ms cap).
claims.excerpt: Every `messages.create` goes out with the SDK per-request option `{ maxRetries: 0 }`, so the SDK never retries underneath the wrapper.

claims.claim: isExportedSymbol is exported from src/extraction/pipeline.ts (was private) so Stream B filter logic is shared between CLI's extractDocstringsForFile and list-extraction-sources, preventing future filter divergence.
claims.rationale: Single-source-of-truth for source-discovery filter across CLI and Skill paths.
claims.excerpt: **isExportedSymbol** exported from `src/extraction/pipeline.ts` (was private). Shared Stream B filter logic between CLI's extractDocstringsForFile and list-extraction-sources prevents future filter divergence

claims.claim: From v1.2 Phase 2, runExtractionPipeline runs docstring (Stage 6c) and commit (Stage 6d) streams after prose, gated by extraction.streams (default: all three); on files matched by docs.include, CLI skips docstring extraction and extracts as prose with a warning while Skill manifest extracts docstrings.
claims.rationale: Divergence between CLI and Skill on docs.include/source-file overlap is known; L-14 parity bar assumes no overlap.
claims.excerpt: the CLI skips docstring extraction for a source file that a `docs.include` glob also matches, and extracts it as prose instead (with a warning; ADR-12 2026-09-25 Decision 2), while the manifest lists that file's docstrings and `/index-atlas` extracts them

claims.claim: deriveSourceName emits canonical `adr:${basename(absPath)}` convention; earlier frontmatter-id / ADR-NN pattern behavior removed.
claims.rationale: Three-substrate alignment (CLI + Skill + validator) at modern source-name convention.
claims.excerpt: **MIGRATED** `deriveSourceName` at `src/extraction/pipeline.ts:573-586` to emit `adr:${basename(absPath)}` canonical convention matching Skill `/index-atlas` SKILL.md spec + validate-extraction canonical source-field format.

claims.claim: The `contextatlas resolve-symbols` subcommand is a Skill→LSP bridge that resolves claims-only atlases via LSP subprocesses with zero API cost.
claims.rationale: Substrate-consistency mechanism enabling Skill-path atlases to match CLI-path substrate at the symbol layer.
claims.excerpt: `contextatlas resolve-symbols` CLI subcommand (`src/extraction/cli-resolve-symbols.ts`): Skill→LSP bridge... Zero API cost (local LSP subprocess only).

claims.claim: A stop_reason of "max_tokens" or "model_context_window_exceeded" now raises an actionable truncation error; no ADRs are written and tokens billed are reported.

claims.excerpt: A `stop_reason` of `"max_tokens"` or `"model_context_window_exceeded"` now raises an actionable truncation error: no ADRs are written, and the tokens billed are reported.

claims.claim: The CLI generate-adrs call uses anthropic.messages.stream with thinking: { type: "adaptive" } and output_config: { effort: "xhigh" }, streamed via finalMessage(); previous budget_tokens: 32_000 parameter is rejected by claude-opus-4-7.

claims.excerpt: SDK 0.128.0 refuses, client-side, a non-streaming request whose `max_tokens` implies more than 10 minutes (`calculateNonstreamingTimeout`; the threshold is about 21.3k tokens).

claims.rationale: Removal eliminates the bash-familiar alternative that agents chose over Read tool; forces canonical prompt-load path.
claims.excerpt: **REMOVED** the deprecated `contextatlas show-prompt` + `contextatlas show-generate-prompt` CLI subcommands entirely. No backward-compat path.

claims.claim: Two extraction entry points coexist: CLI (`contextatlas index`) uses Anthropic API direct pay-per-use, and Claude Code slash command (`/index-atlas`) uses subscription-bounded session tokens.
claims.rationale: Entry-point-determined cost model — surface chosen by user determines cost model.
claims.excerpt: Two extraction entry points coexist... Anthropic API direct path via CLI... Claude Code Skills path via slash command

claims.claim: `contextatlas validate-adrs` validates docs/adr/*.md against canonical depth-floor invariants (frontmatter, sections, ≥2 symbol-with-line-number citations, ≥2 Context paragraphs, ≥2 named alternatives, ≥1 code block, ≥3 Rationale, ≥3 Consequences, 600-line ceiling).
claims.rationale: Mechanical depth-floor for ADR quality; prevents text-only prompt-tightening from binding depth.
claims.excerpt: **ADDED** `contextatlas validate-adrs` CLI subcommand... validates each ADR against canonical depth-floor invariants

claims.claim: `contextatlas validate-extraction` enforces three invariants: adr_claims_present (source starts with "adr:"), adr_depth_floor (≥8 claims per ADR), source_coverage (each ADR-shaped source_shas key has ≥1 matching claim).
claims.rationale: Mechanical depth-floor + coverage catches ADR-stream-skip regressions and silent per-source extraction failure.
claims.excerpt: **ADDED** `contextatlas validate-extraction` CLI subcommand (`src/extraction/cli-validate-extraction.ts`). Parallel pattern to cli-validate-adrs.ts. Three invariants

claims.claim: atlas.json includes cost_usd (numeric Anthropic API cost, $0 for Skills) and cost_model fields ("api" | "subscription-bounded") recording which entry point generated the extraction.
claims.rationale: Cost-accounting reflects entry point for provenance.
claims.excerpt: `cost_usd` field reports numeric Anthropic API cost ($0 for Skills entry point); `cost_model` field captures path semantics (`"api"` | `"subscription-bounded"`) as atlas.json metadata

claims.claim: src/extraction/cli-runner.ts auto-invokes validate-extraction post-pipeline; guarded so atlasExported prevents re-validation on SHA-diff incremental skips and clientOverride skips under test mode.
claims.rationale: Closes CLI-vs-Skill mechanical-floor-enforcement substrate equivalence at /index-atlas surface.
claims.excerpt: CLI substrate-equivalent change: `src/extraction/cli-runner.ts` auto-invokes `validate-extraction` post-pipeline (parallel pattern to Step 2.4.a β-2 validate-adrs auto-invoke at generation cli-runner).

claims.claim: src/generation/generators/anthropic-api-direct.ts imports @anthropic-ai/sdk but is not currently listed in the permitted-modules invariant; index-time only so query-time invariant is unaffected, but the permitted-modules rule text is unchanged (open ADR decision).
claims.rationale: Records a known drift between permitted-modules rule text and shipped generator client.
claims.excerpt: The generator client in (e), `src/generation/generators/anthropic-api-direct.ts`, has imported it since v0.7 Step 2.2.a.2... and no later permitted-modules extension names it, so that grep returns one match.

claims.claim: Adapter loading is centralized in a single bootstrap location (src/index.ts or src/adapters/registry.ts) that reads config and injects adapters into core.
claims.rationale: Single point of adapter instantiation enables dependency injection and isolates the registry change required to add a language.
claims.excerpt: Adapter loading happens in one place: the bootstrap code in `src/index.ts` (or a dedicated `src/adapters/registry.ts`).

claims.claim: Adapters must not share state with each other; each operates independently within its language.
claims.rationale: Shared state would couple adapters and break pluggability.
claims.excerpt: Adapters must not share state with each other.

claims.claim: ContextAtlas supports TypeScript and Python in MVP with a roadmap to Java, Go, .NET, and Rust, each as a separate adapter module wrapping a language server.
claims.rationale: Explains the motivation for a pluggable adapter architecture.
claims.excerpt: ContextAtlas supports TypeScript and Python in MVP, with a roadmap to Java, Go, .NET, and Rust.

claims.claim: Cross-adapter assumptions are disallowed; code that works for one language but not another is a design bug and the logic must move into the adapter or the interface must expose the capability.
claims.rationale: Prevents implicit coupling to specific languages from leaking into core or other adapters.
claims.excerpt: Cross-adapter assumptions are disallowed.

claims.claim: Dependency injection is required throughout: functions needing a language adapter receive it as a parameter rather than importing one directly.
claims.rationale: Direct imports would violate the core-does-not-know-adapters rule.
claims.excerpt: Functions that need a language adapter receive it as a parameter, never import it directly.

claims.claim: Tests can substitute mock adapters without monkey-patching due to the injection-based design.
claims.rationale: Testability benefit of the decision.
claims.excerpt: Tests can substitute mock adapters without monkey-patching.

claims.claim: Adding a new language adapter requires only a new file in src/adapters/ implementing LanguageAdapter, one line in the registry, and tests; no other files should change.
claims.rationale: Defines the closed/open boundary for extending language support.
claims.excerpt: No other file in the codebase should need to change.

claims.claim: Core code must import only the LanguageAdapter interface from src/types.ts and must not import concrete adapter implementations.
claims.rationale: Prevents core from depending on specific adapters, keeping language support truly pluggable rather than a switch statement.
claims.excerpt: Core code MUST NOT import concrete adapter implementations.

claims.claim: The LanguageAdapter interface is treated as stable public API; changes are protocol-level and break all adapter implementations.
claims.rationale: Third-party adapters depend on interface stability.
claims.excerpt: Treat interface changes like protocol changes.

claims.claim: Any new field added to bundles must define both its JSON shape and its compact representation.
claims.rationale: Adding only one representation is explicitly called out as a bug.
claims.excerpt: Any new field added to bundles requires defining both its JSON shape and its compact representation. Adding only one is a bug.

claims.claim: Automated tools that need to parse bundle output should request format: "json" rather than parsing compact output.
claims.rationale: The compact parser on the receiving side is informal and unsuitable for automated parsing.
claims.excerpt: If a future automated tool needs to parse compact output, it should request `format: "json"` instead.

claims.claim: Bundle size concerns should be addressed via progressive disclosure with IDs, not by switching output formats.
claims.rationale: Format choice is not the remedy for oversized responses.
claims.excerpt: Bundle size advice (avoid huge responses) applies to both formats. The fix is progressive disclosure via IDs, not format choice.

claims.claim: Changes to the compact grammar require a minor version bump.
claims.rationale: The compact grammar is part of DESIGN.md and is treated as a versioned interface.
claims.excerpt: The compact grammar is part of DESIGN.md and changes require a minor version bump.

claims.claim: Compact text is the default output format for get_symbol_context and all future bundle-returning tools.
claims.rationale: Token efficiency is the core value proposition; defaulting to JSON would undercut the tool's purpose of reducing tool-call burn.
claims.excerpt: Compact text is the default output format for `get_symbol_context` and all future bundle-returning tools.

claims.claim: JSON output is available by passing format: "json" in input parameters.
claims.rationale: Provides programmatic consumers (benchmark harnesses, future UI) an opt-in alternative.
claims.excerpt: JSON is available by passing `format: "json"` in the input parameters.

claims.claim: The JSON schema is stable public API documented in src/types.ts (SymbolContextBundle).
claims.rationale: JSON is the stable contract for programmatic consumers.
claims.excerpt: The JSON schema is stable public API documented in `src/types.ts` (`SymbolContextBundle`).

claims.claim: The compact format is parsed informally by an LLM consumer, not a formal parser; the grammar must be tight enough to avoid information loss.
claims.rationale: Explains tolerance for minor formatting inconsistencies but the need for grammar discipline.
claims.excerpt: The compact grammar is parsed by Claude's LLM, not by a formal parser. Minor formatting inconsistencies are tolerated by the consumer, but the grammar must be tight enough that Claude doesn't lose information.

claims.claim: Config errors for extraction.streams: not a list (including null), empty list, non-string entry, wrong value or wrong case, duplicate entries, or list missing `adr`
claims.rationale: Each condition is a config error naming the config file
claims.excerpt: Each of these is a config error naming the config file

claims.claim: A docstring key whose file no longer exists is always deleted; deletion of keys for files that exist but are no longer walked applies only while the docstring stream runs
claims.rationale: Amends ADR-12 (2026-09-25) to scope the walked-file deletion rule to when the stream is enabled
claims.excerpt: The v1.2 Phase 2 rule that also deletes the key of a file that exists but is no longer walked applies only while the docstring stream runs

claims.claim: Adding additive optional keys does not bump the `version` field in practice; version is reserved for breaking changes
claims.rationale: Every optional key added since the first parser kept version: 1; configs that loaded before still load
claims.excerpt: Additive optional keys stay `version: 1`.

claims.claim: Config file must be YAML, not JSON, TOML, or TS
claims.rationale: YAML is the standard for dev-tool config files (GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, CircleCI); avoids less-familiar formats
claims.excerpt: MUST be YAML. Not JSON, not TOML, not a TS file.

claims.claim: Config file must be at the repo root, not a subdirectory or dotfile elsewhere
claims.rationale: Enforces predictable discovery location
claims.excerpt: MUST be in the repo root. Not a subdirectory, not a dotfile elsewhere.

claims.claim: Config inheritance (extends), cross-repo references (imports-from), monorepo workspace awareness, and environment-specific overrides are explicitly rejected features
claims.rationale: Reintroducing these would be a v1.0+ conversation, not a v0.x field addition
claims.excerpt: Features that might seem reasonable but are explicitly rejected

claims.claim: Config must validate against declared schema; unknown top-level keys are errors, not warnings
claims.rationale: Strict schema validation surfaces config bugs at startup, not at runtime when a missing key causes unexpected behavior
claims.excerpt: MUST validate against the declared schema. Unknown top-level keys are errors, not warnings.

claims.claim: Disabling a stream gates extraction but preserves existing claims: claims and source_shas of disabled streams remain frozen in the atlas and are still returned by queries
claims.rationale: The key gates extraction, not content
claims.excerpt: Disabling a stream keeps its claims. The key gates extraction, not content.

claims.claim: Monorepo users with multiple distinct projects need multiple configs (one per project root)
claims.rationale: Accepted consequence of the single-file-per-repo rule
claims.excerpt: Monorepo users with multiple distinct projects need multiple configs (one per project root). This is accepted.

claims.claim: Older contextatlas binaries (pre-v1.2 Phase 2) reject `extraction.streams` as an unknown key; teams on mixed versions should omit the key until everyone upgrades
claims.rationale: Unknown keys are errors under strict schema validation
claims.excerpt: A team on mixed versions should leave the key out until everyone has upgraded.

claims.claim: Streams always run in fixed order adr → docstring → commit regardless of list order
claims.rationale: Prose runs first so its 'every document failed' error can never discard a later stream's paid work
claims.excerpt: the streams always run in the fixed order adr → docstring → commit

claims.claim: Teams wanting shared config across repos must copy or symlink; no framework-level inheritance is provided
claims.rationale: Consequence of rejecting inheritance
claims.excerpt: Teams that want a shared config across repos must copy it, or use symlinks. No framework-level inheritance.

claims.claim: The `version: 1` field is the migration handle for future breaking changes and must be treated as sacred
claims.rationale: It is the sole mechanism for handling future breaking changes
claims.excerpt: The `version: 1` field at the top of the config is the migration handle for future breaking changes. Treat it as sacred.

claims.claim: When `extraction.streams` is absent, all three streams run; the default is applied at use site in resolveExtractionStreams, not written into the parsed config; `contextatlas init` writes no `streams` key
claims.rationale: Keeps parsed config faithful to user input; centralizes default resolution
claims.excerpt: The default is applied where the value is used (`resolveExtractionStreams` in `src/config/streams.ts`), not written into the parsed config.

claims.claim: With a stream disabled the manifest becomes `manifest_version: "2"`, which pre-v1.2 /index-atlas versions refuse rather than misinterpreting empty arrays as deleted sources
claims.rationale: Prevents older Skill versions from destructively interpreting the new empty-array semantics
claims.excerpt: the manifest is `manifest_version: "2"`, which `/index-atlas` copies from before v1.2 refuse, instead of reading the empty arrays as deleted sources

claims.claim: Without `extraction.streams`, `contextatlas index` makes docstring and commit model calls by default (including init's first run); a cost preview is printed to stderr first; `streams: [adr]` restores prose-only extraction
claims.rationale: Documents cost implications of the default behavior change
claims.excerpt: Without the key, `contextatlas index` now makes docstring and commit model calls by default, including `init`'s first run.

claims.claim: `adr` is required in extraction.streams because `index` runs `validate-extraction` after every exporting run, whose invariants need ADR claims
claims.rationale: Docstring and commit streams are the real cost levers; the adr requirement can be relaxed later without breaking existing configs
claims.excerpt: `adr` is required because `index` runs `validate-extraction` after every exporting run, and its invariants need ADR claims.

claims.claim: `contextatlas doctor` reports enabled streams via `config.extraction_streams` and warns when atlas.json holds claims of a disabled stream
claims.rationale: Surfaces stale disabled-stream content to operators
claims.excerpt: `contextatlas doctor` reports the enabled streams (`config.extraction_streams`) and warns when `atlas.json` still holds claims of a disabled stream.

claims.claim: `contextatlas list-extraction-sources` emits empty arrays for disabled streams and names them in `summary.disabled_streams`; /index-atlas keeps disabled-stream keys frozen except when the source file no longer exists
claims.rationale: Skill path must honour the streams key consistently with CLI
claims.excerpt: The Skill path honours the key too.

claims.claim: `extraction.streams` is an optional list with values `adr`, `docstring`, `commit` (lowercase)
claims.rationale: Defines the config gate that lets teams turn docstring and commit streams off to control cost
claims.excerpt: `extraction.streams` is an optional list

claims.claim: Adding a new config field is a deliberate decision requiring version bump, DESIGN.md documentation, and ContextAtlasConfig type update
claims.rationale: Prevents scope creep in configuration surface
claims.excerpt: Adding a new config field is a deliberate decision — bumps the `version` field, documented in DESIGN.md, added to `ContextAtlasConfig` type.

claims.claim: Configuration must be a single .contextatlas.yml file at the repo root; no includes, imports, or inheritance chains
claims.rationale: A single file is greppable, copyable, reviewable in one PR; no inheritance avoids debugging which config is active
claims.excerpt: MUST be a single file. No includes, no imports, no inheritance chains.

claims.claim: Atlas propagates distilled ADR content; default committed:true assumes ADRs are already committed so no new exposure is added
claims.rationale: Privacy assumption should be documented but not enforced — teams know their own privacy situation
claims.excerpt: This assumption should be documented but not enforced — teams know their own privacy situation.

claims.claim: Atlas schema is versioned public API; breaking changes require a major version bump and automatic v1-to-v2 migration
claims.rationale: Users should not have to regenerate atlases by hand when the schema evolves
claims.excerpt: Migration from v1 to v2 must be handled automatically — users should not have to regenerate atlases by hand.

claims.claim: AtlasExporter and AtlasImporter must be lossless: round-tripping a canonical atlas must be a no-op
claims.rationale: Bidirectional sync between SQLite and atlas.json requires perfect fidelity to maintain the canonical artifact
claims.excerpt: Both must be lossless — round-tripping a canonical atlas must be a no-op.

claims.claim: CI should flag drift when ADR/code edits don't update atlas.json; a pre-commit hook should regenerate atlas.json when relevant files change
claims.rationale: Keeping atlas.json synchronized with source is a tooling requirement to maintain the reviewable artifact
claims.excerpt: If a developer edits an ADR and doesn't update atlas.json, CI should flag the drift.

claims.claim: Chunking atlas.json (e.g., one file per source ADR) may be a future enhancement for very large repos
claims.rationale: Megabyte-sized atlases handle in git but degrade diff review experience
claims.excerpt: For very large repos, chunking atlas.json (one file per source ADR, for example) may be a future enhancement.

claims.claim: Every source file indexed must have its SHA recorded in atlas.json for incremental reindex to function
claims.rationale: Without SHA tracking the system cannot distinguish unchanged from changed files, leading to wasted re-extraction or missed updates
claims.excerpt: SHA tracking is load-bearing.

claims.claim: Future minor version bumps MUST add only optional omit-when-absent fields, follow round-trip nullish convention, and leave earlier-version atlases readable unmodified
claims.rationale: The omit-when-absent rule preserves back-compat; anything else constitutes a major bump
claims.excerpt: any future minor bump MUST add only optional fields, MUST follow the round-trip nullish convention

claims.claim: atlas.json is self-describing: includes generator version, model used, and SHAs of all source files
claims.rationale: Self-describing artifact supports auditability and incremental reindex
claims.excerpt: Self-describing: includes generator version, model used, and SHAs of all source files it was built from

claims.claim: atlas.json is the committed team artifact, human-readable JSON at .contextatlas/atlas.json by default
claims.rationale: Committed artifact enables zero-onboarding cost, PR review, and canonical extraction shared across team
claims.excerpt: atlas.json — the committed team artifact

claims.claim: atlas.json must use deterministic ordering: symbols sorted by ID, claims sorted by (source, symbol_id, claim), arrays in stable order
claims.rationale: Non-determinism creates noise in git diffs and undermines the reviewable-artifact property
claims.excerpt: Deterministic ordering is a hard requirement.

claims.claim: atlas.json schema stability is stricter than internal SQLite schema; keep atlas schema narrow enough to be stable
claims.rationale: atlas.json is user-visible and committed, so changes require user coordination, unlike SQLite which can evolve via migrations
claims.excerpt: Keep the atlas schema narrow enough to be stable.

claims.claim: committed:false must be a first-class supported mode, with testing covering both modes
claims.rationale: Some teams legitimately cannot commit the atlas (regulated environments, internal-only code); system must work correctly, not just degrade
claims.excerpt: The system must work correctly in this mode, not just "work but lose the team benefit."

claims.claim: index.db is a local derived cache, SQLite, gitignored and never committed; rebuilt from atlas.json on demand
claims.rationale: SQLite is binary and unreviewable; it serves query-time performance only and must not be the source of truth
claims.excerpt: **Gitignored** — never committed

claims.claim: Config exposes committed/path/local_cache options; committed:true is the default
claims.rationale: The commit-or-not decision is surfaced as a deliberate config choice for teams with privacy/compliance needs
claims.excerpt: committed: true          # default; commits atlas.json

claims.claim: A getTypeInfo call costs roughly 1 hover + 1 implementation + up to N documentSymbol requests for N descendants; cross-call caching is post-MVP.
claims.rationale: Acceptable at bundle-build time; caching is gated on benchmark evidence.
claims.excerpt: a cross-call cache is post-MVP and gated on benchmark evidence.

claims.claim: Adapters must not throw for symbols with no type relationships; they must return empty arrays.
claims.rationale: Empty arrays are valid returns for utility functions, standalone classes, and marker interfaces.
claims.excerpt: Adapters MUST NOT throw for symbols that have no relationships; they return `{ extends: [], implements: [], usedByTypes: [] }`.

claims.claim: Every LanguageAdapter implementation must implement getTypeInfo as a required method.
claims.rationale: Type relationships are core to impact_of_change and get_symbol_context tools; a stubbed implementation would produce silently-wrong results.
claims.excerpt: Every future adapter MUST implement `getTypeInfo`.

claims.claim: The TypeScript adapter implements getTypeInfo using textDocument/hover for extends/implements and textDocument/implementation for usedByTypes.
claims.rationale: These are standard LSP requests implemented by typescript-language-server and Pyright, providing a uniform facade across languages.
claims.excerpt: The TypeScript adapter implements `getTypeInfo` via the language server

claims.claim: Type-relationship extraction lives in the adapter layer, not the storage layer, because storage has no language grammar.
claims.rationale: The storage layer holds symbol IDs and claims but lacks TypeScript or Python grammar; the language server has this knowledge.
claims.excerpt: Neither tool can compute type relationships generically at the storage layer.

claims.claim: A hover-format canary test should exist in the adapter's test suite to catch tsserver hover-format changes at CI time.
claims.rationale: tsserver's hover markdown has varied across major versions and could break the permissive parser in the future.
claims.excerpt: A hover-format canary test in the adapter's test suite catches this at CI time rather than at runtime.

claims.claim: Callers should treat empty usedByTypes as 'no known children at this moment,' not as an absolute claim.
claims.rationale: Accuracy is LSP-state-dependent; language servers only return inverse references for analyzed files, and edge cases like crashes or excludeDirs can produce under-reporting.
claims.excerpt: callers that act on `usedByTypes` should treat empty results as "no known children at this moment," not as an absolute claim.

claims.claim: The LanguageAdapter contract is treated as public API; getTypeInfo is defined before multiple adapters exist to avoid retrofitting.
claims.rationale: Adding methods to a public adapter interface after multiple adapters exist requires touching every implementation.
claims.excerpt: the `LanguageAdapter` contract is public API. Adding `getTypeInfo` after implementations exist means retrofitting.

claims.claim: Any change to TypeInfo is a breaking change requiring a major version bump.
claims.rationale: The adapter interface is a stable public contract.
claims.excerpt: Any change to `TypeInfo` is a breaking change requiring a major version bump.

claims.claim: Generic constraints are excluded from extends/implements; balanced <...> spans are stripped before token extraction.
claims.rationale: Matches developer intent and how reviewers read the code; e.g., class Box<T extends Widget> does not register Widget as a parent of Box.
claims.excerpt: Generic constraints are excluded from `extends` / `implements`.

claims.claim: The compact bundle formatter (step 6) reads TypeInfo directly, so TypeInfo changes propagate to the renderer and committed atlas fixtures.
claims.rationale: Coupling between TypeInfo shape and the renderer/fixtures must be considered when modifying TypeInfo.
claims.excerpt: A change to `TypeInfo` propagates to the renderer and any committed atlas fixtures.

claims.claim: usedByTypes returns direct children only; transitive closure is not returned.
claims.rationale: Matches tsserver's textDocument/implementation default behavior and prevents adapters from disagreeing on transitivity.
claims.excerpt: Direct children only — transitive closure is not returned.

claims.claim: A round-trip canary test asserts the main repo's committed atlas survives storage code changes byte-identically.
claims.rationale: Guards against accidental drift breaking the 'existing atlases read unchanged' promise.
claims.excerpt: A round-trip canary test asserts the main repo's own committed atlas survives storage code changes byte-identically.

claims.claim: ADR aggregation across locations is undefined; colliding ADR identifiers have undefined behavior and callers must deduplicate before invoking.
claims.rationale: No merge semantics implemented for combining ADR trees.
claims.excerpt: behavior is undefined; aggregation callers must deduplicate before invoking ContextAtlas.

claims.claim: ADRs must be readable from the filesystem; URL-, archive-, or VCS-protocol-based sources are out of scope.
claims.rationale: Constrains ADR ingestion surface.
claims.excerpt: ADRs must be readable from the filesystem.

claims.claim: Absolute --config values bypass configRoot for file location but do not change how atlas.path and source.root inside the config resolve — those remain relative to configRoot.
claims.rationale: Keeps in-config path semantics consistent regardless of how the config file itself was located.
claims.excerpt: Absolute values of `--config` bypass `configRoot` for file location but do not change how paths inside that config resolve

claims.claim: Atlas format version stays at '1.0'; existing atlases read and round-trip unchanged.
claims.rationale: Backward compatibility for committed atlases.
claims.excerpt: Atlas format version stays at `"1.0"`. Existing atlases read and round-trip unchanged.

claims.claim: Atlases are source-root-specific; relocating ADRs across source roots requires re-extraction.
claims.rationale: SHAs and path contexts change across source roots, so portability is not supported.
claims.excerpt: An atlas generated against source root A cannot be used as-is against source root B.

claims.claim: MCP runtime binary accepts --config-root <path> CLI flag; defaults to process.cwd(); unknown flags and missing/empty values reject with actionable errors.
claims.rationale: Avoids silent fallback to cwd on typos, ensuring config-root selection is explicit.
claims.excerpt: Unknown flags and missing/empty values reject with actionable errors; there's no silent fallback to cwd on typos.

claims.claim: Only one adrs.path per config is supported; multiple ADR roots are not provided.
claims.rationale: Aggregation across sources must be done externally; not part of this ADR.
claims.excerpt: Only one `adrs.path` per config.

claims.claim: Runtime source.root is declared in the config file rather than passed as a function argument, unlike extraction-side configRoot.
claims.rationale: MCP clients pass only CLI args and env; config file is the natural place to pin source location.
claims.excerpt: the runtime `source.root` is declared in the config file rather than passed as a function argument

claims.claim: adrs.path may resolve outside the source root, accepting relative-under-root, absolute, or traversal paths.
claims.rationale: Decouples ADR location from source location to support shared/external architecture repos.
claims.excerpt: `adrs.path` in `.contextatlas.yml` may resolve to a location outside the source root.

claims.claim: adrs.path must name a directory; single-ADR-file configurations are not supported.
claims.rationale: Wrap a single file in a directory rather than pointing adrs.path at a file.
claims.excerpt: `adrs.path` must name a directory. Single-ADR-file configurations are not supported

claims.claim: config.source.root, when present, resolves relative to configRoot or absolute; when absent, the adapter initializes against configRoot.
claims.rationale: Matches today's single-root flow when source.root is unset.
claims.excerpt: `config.source.root` (when present, relative to configRoot or absolute) tells the adapter where source code lives.

claims.claim: source_path values in atlas.json follow a two-branch rule: stored relative to repoRoot when under repoRoot, otherwise relative to the ADR base directory (for ADR bucket) or configRoot (for docs bucket).
claims.rationale: Deterministic stored-path rule preserves backward compatibility with existing committed atlases.
claims.excerpt: `source_path` values in `atlas.json` follow a deterministic two-branch rule

claims.claim: Source-file walking continues to use repoRoot and remains strictly enforced under the source root; only prose-file walking (ADRs + docs) is affected by configRoot.
claims.rationale: Preserves ID-stability and security invariants from ADR-01 for source files.
claims.excerpt: Source-file walking continues to use `repoRoot`. The source-under-source-root invariant from ADR-01 stays intact.

claims.claim: walkProseFiles signature gains an optional third argument for configRoot; callers passing only the first two retain current behavior.
claims.rationale: Backward-compatible API extension.
claims.excerpt: `walkProseFiles` signature gains an optional third argument for `configRoot`.

claims.claim: runExtractionPipeline accepts an optional configRoot dep that bases adrs.path and docs.include resolution; defaults to repoRoot.
claims.rationale: Separates config-relative path resolution from source-root resolution while preserving backward compatibility.
claims.excerpt: The pipeline accepts a new optional `configRoot` parameter on `runExtractionPipeline`'s deps.

claims.claim: toRelativePath stays strict and continues to enforce 'under root' for source files.
claims.rationale: Identity for source code requires canonicalization to a single known root; the relaxation only applies to prose files.
claims.excerpt: `toRelativePath` stays strict and continues to enforce "under root" for source files.

claims.claim: Atlas round-trip remains lossless: atlas.json contains claims only; FTS index is derived locally
claims.rationale: Preserves lossless serialization invariant; FTS is a derived index not part of the exported atlas
claims.excerpt: Atlas round-trip stays lossless: `atlas.json` contains claims only; FTS is a derived local index.

claims.claim: BM25 + FTS5 ranking primitives are reused by get_symbol_context's intent block when an optional query is provided (ADR-16)
claims.rationale: ADR-16 documents shared ranking primitives across tools
claims.excerpt: BM25 extension to `get_symbol_context` — DELIVERED in [ADR-16]

claims.claim: Compact output uses SYM, SIG, INTENT vocabulary matching get_symbol_context
claims.rationale: LLMs familiar with primitive output can parse it without re-learning
claims.excerpt: matches `get_symbol_context`'s vocabulary — `SYM`, `SIG`, `INTENT` — so LLMs familiar with primitive output parse it without re-learning

claims.claim: Empty query after sanitization returns MATCHES 0 with a hint, not an error
claims.rationale: Matches primitive's render-cleanly-when-empty pattern
claims.excerpt: Empty query after sanitization (e.g. `"!!!"` → ""): tool returns `MATCHES 0` with a hint in the compact text, not an error.

claims.claim: Name-overlap tiebreaker fix is implemented in src/queries/find-by-intent.ts with a regression test locking the scenario
claims.rationale: Documents where the fix lives and that it is regression-protected
claims.excerpt: The fix is ~15 lines in `src/queries/find-by-intent.ts` plus a regression test locking the scenario.

claims.claim: Queries are sanitized (non-alphanumeric stripped to spaces) and built as MATCH string: "<exact phrase>" OR word1 OR word2
claims.rationale: Single MATCH string lets BM25 do phrase-vs-scatter weighting in one query
claims.excerpt: Queries are sanitized (non-alphanumeric stripped to spaces) and passed to FTS5 via the `MATCH` operator

claims.claim: Query sanitization strips FTS5 MATCH operators; users cannot pass MATCH syntax directly
claims.rationale: Deliberate constraint — user input is natural language; advanced query DSL is post-MVP
claims.excerpt: Users cannot pass FTS5 MATCH syntax directly (no manual `"phrase"`, `col:word`, `NEAR()`). This is a deliberate constraint

claims.claim: Response deliberately omits numeric relevance score; rank is implicit in array order
claims.rationale: BM25 scores aren't calibrated across queries; surfacing them would read as false-precision probability
claims.excerpt: Deliberately **no `relevance` score** in the response. BM25 scores aren't calibrated across queries

claims.claim: Response format follows primitive convention: compact text by default, JSON opt-in via format parameter (default 'compact')
claims.rationale: Unified vocabulary across tools lets consumers pick format once rather than per-tool
claims.excerpt: Mirrors the primitive's convention: compact text by default, JSON opt-in via a `format` input parameter

claims.claim: Results ordered by bm25(claims_fts) ASC (more negative = more relevant) with LIMIT for pagination
claims.rationale: BM25 returns negative scores where lower is more relevant; ascending sort gives best-first
claims.excerpt: The query `ORDER BY bm25(claims_fts) ASC LIMIT ?` gives best-first truncated to the requested page.

claims.claim: Source column is not indexed in FTS; it is an identifier-shaped filter, not a search axis
claims.rationale: Identifier-shaped fields produce noise in natural-language FTS; filtering by source is post-MVP
claims.excerpt: Source is **not** indexed in FTS. It's an identifier-shaped filter ("ADR-07"), not a search axis.

claims.claim: Tokenizer behavior superseded by ADR-17: v0.3+ uses tokenchars '_-' plus dual-form indexing to support snake_case and kebab-case identifiers
claims.rationale: v0.1 default unicode61 tokenizer silently buried snake_case and kebab-case identifiers; ADR-17 reconfigures the tokenizer
claims.excerpt: Tokenizer behavior — superseded by [ADR-17]...ADR-17 changes the tokenizer to keep `_` and `-` inside tokens and adds dual-form indexing

claims.claim: Zero matches render as `MATCHES 0 [query="..."]` with no body lines, consistent with primitive's 'omit empty sections' rule
claims.rationale: Consistent empty-state rendering across primitives
claims.excerpt: Zero matches render as `MATCHES 0 [query="..."]` with no body lines

claims.claim: claims_fts is a FTS5 virtual table indexing claim + rationale + excerpt columns of the claims table, maintained by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers
claims.rationale: Defines the indexing substrate and how it stays in sync with the base table
claims.excerpt: A virtual table `claims_fts` indexes the `claim + rationale + excerpt` text columns of the `claims` table. The FTS index is maintained by triggers

claims.claim: find_by_intent is a thin composite over the claims table, not a new infrastructure layer
claims.rationale: Per DESIGN.md, the tool composes existing primitives rather than introducing new infrastructure
claims.excerpt: Per DESIGN.md this is a thin composite over the claims table — not a new infrastructure layer.

claims.claim: find_by_intent must not make query-time LLM/Anthropic API calls or use embeddings; ranking is 100% local SQL + FTS5 BM25
claims.rationale: ADR-02 forbids Anthropic API calls outside the extraction pipeline; this bound must hold
claims.excerpt: ADR-02 forbids Anthropic API calls outside the extraction pipeline. This tool's ranking is 100% SQL + FTS5 BM25, executed locally

claims.claim: find_by_intent searches claims, not symbol metadata; callers who know a symbol name should use get_symbol_context
claims.rationale: Tool scope is claim-content search; symbol-name lookup is a different primitive
claims.excerpt: `find_by_intent` is a claims search, not a symbol-name search, a user who knows the symbol name by literal form should use `get_symbol_context` directly

claims.claim: limit input defaults to 5, max 50; no offset/cursor pagination for MVP
claims.rationale: Single-page semantics keep tool response bounded and composable
claims.excerpt: `limit` input, default 5, max 50. ... No `offset` / cursor for MVP.

claims.claim: v0.1 may return clustered top-N results from one module; no diversity post-processing applied
claims.rationale: Diversity heuristics are post-MVP and evidence-gated
claims.excerpt: v0.1 may return clustered top-N results when a query term appears densely in nearby files

claims.claim: Tiebreaker chain: BM25 asc, then name-overlap desc, then severity (hard>soft>context), then source alphabetical, then claim id
claims.rationale: Deterministic ordering aligned with buildBundle's severity ordering for consistent caller experience
claims.excerpt: Severity:** `hard > soft > context`. Matches the primitive's intent ordering in `buildBundle`

claims.claim: insertClaim, deleteClaimsBySourcePath, importAtlas need no changes; triggers keep FTS in sync; canary test verifies FTS row count matches claims row count
claims.rationale: Trigger-based maintenance avoids touching write paths and a canary test enforces the invariant
claims.excerpt: `insertClaim` / `deleteClaimsBySourcePath` / `importAtlas` do not need changes — the triggers keep FTS in sync automatically. A canary test verifies FTS row count matches `claims` row count

claims.claim: Name-overlap tiebreaker added to resolve ADR-08 frontmatter-hint interactions where multiple symbols share identical claim, score, severity, source, and id
claims.rationale: ADR-08 auto-links one claim to every symbol the source ADR's frontmatter declares, causing ties that the original chain couldn't break
claims.excerpt: the original three-level tiebreaker chain couldn't distinguish them, so query `normalizePath` returned arbitrary ordering where name-match should rank first

claims.claim: 500-commit window is a hard cap per-extraction, not per-symbol; unbounded-history ingestion is a non-goal.
claims.rationale: Cap prevents unbounded growth on long-lived repos while covering typical multi-quarter history.
claims.excerpt: 500 commits is the cap.

claims.claim: A file is hot when it appears in ≥ config.git.recentCommits distinct commits within the 500-commit extraction window.
claims.rationale: One config knob serves both the recent-commits display and hotness threshold.
claims.excerpt: A file is **hot** when it appears in `≥ config.git.recentCommits` distinct commits within the 500-commit extraction window.

claims.claim: A pre-computed git_cochange cache table is deliberately NOT shipped for v0.1; self-join is fast enough.
claims.rationale: Premature optimization; cache would add invalidation complexity without measured need.
claims.excerpt: A pre-computed `git_cochange` cache table is deliberately **not** shipped for v0.1

claims.claim: Atlas stores git_commits with embedded files arrays; local SQLite cache derives git_file_commits on import by flattening arrays.
claims.rationale: Saves atlas bytes and provides a pre-indexed file-pivoted table for query.
claims.excerpt: the local cache **derives** `git_file_commits` on import by flattening those arrays

claims.claim: Attribution is file-level only; symbol→git mapping is one-hop via symbol.path. No line-range blame or hunk heuristics.
claims.rationale: Line-level blame is expensive, unstable under formatting churn, and wrong under refactors; file-level matches user questions.
claims.excerpt: Git operates on files. The symbol → git mapping is **one-hop via `symbol.path`**.

claims.claim: ContextAtlas ships primitives only and does not prescribe a staleness/update workflow.
claims.rationale: Teams compose their own workflow from `--check`, re-extract, commit primitives.
claims.excerpt: ContextAtlas ships the primitives (`--check`, re-run extraction, commit the regenerated atlas) and deliberately does not prescribe a workflow.

claims.claim: Elapsed-days hotness threshold is rejected because it re-introduces a clock dependency at query time.
claims.rationale: Index-time freezes the window at extraction; calendar-based thresholds misreport idle-then-active repos.
claims.excerpt: rejected because it re-introduces a clock dependency at query time

claims.claim: Extraction records current git HEAD SHA in atlas.extracted_at_sha; field is optional on read so pre-1.1 atlases load unchanged, always written on extract.
claims.rationale: Backward-compatible read with forward-only write enables staleness detection.
claims.excerpt: The field is optional on read so pre-1.1 atlases load unchanged; it is always written on extract.

claims.claim: Extraction runs `git log -500 --no-merges --name-only --pretty=...` against repoRoot; merge commits are dropped.
claims.rationale: Merge commits inflate co-change without representing real edits; 500-commit window bounds growth.
claims.excerpt: Merge commits are dropped — they inflate co-change without representing real edits.

claims.claim: Git always runs against repoRoot, never configRoot.
claims.rationale: Source paths and source-file git history live together; symmetric to ADR-08's source-vs-prose split.
claims.excerpt: Git always runs against **`repoRoot`**, never `configRoot`.

claims.claim: Git data is extracted at index time and served from storage; no MCP tool shells out to git at query time.
claims.rationale: Query-time git would spawn subprocesses per call; index-time gives deterministic offline-reproducible atlas and cheap query latency.
claims.excerpt: No MCP tool shells out to `git` at query time.

claims.claim: Git signal re-extraction is full each run, not SHA-incremental; the git phase always rebuilds git_commits and git_file_commits from a fresh git log.
claims.rationale: Subprocess is fast; full rebuild side-steps force-push/rebase edge cases that incremental merges introduce.
claims.excerpt: The git phase always rebuilds `git_commits` + `git_file_commits` from a fresh `git log` on every extraction run.

claims.claim: If repoRoot is not inside a git working tree, the git phase logs a warning and records zero commits; pipeline completes without hard failure.
claims.rationale: Git absence is a legitimate state (fresh checkout, tarballs) that shouldn't block extraction.
claims.excerpt: No hard failure — git absence is a legitimate state

claims.claim: No flag in v0.1 chains --check with auto-extraction; teams script `--check` + `contextatlas index` themselves.
claims.rationale: Forced re-indexing on staleness is out of scope for v0.1.
claims.excerpt: no flag chains the check with auto-extraction in v0.1

claims.claim: Non-git VCS backends (hg, fossil, svn) are out of scope; supporting them requires a separate ADR.
claims.rationale: Extractor shells out to git; other VCS would need their own extraction path.
claims.excerpt: `hg`, `fossil`, `svn` are out.

claims.claim: Prose extraction remains SHA-incremental because Opus-backed stages are expensive; only expensive stages pay the unchanged-skip optimization.
claims.rationale: Cost asymmetry justifies different reuse strategies for prose vs git.
claims.excerpt: Prose extraction remains SHA-incremental per DESIGN.md — only Opus-backed stages pay the unchanged-skip optimization

claims.claim: Query-time `git log` calls are a hard boundary; if a query needs fresh git data, user re-runs extraction.
claims.rationale: Preserves index-time discipline and avoids per-query subprocess cost.
claims.excerpt: **Query-time `git log` calls.** Hard boundary.

claims.claim: Schema migration v3 is additive — no touches to v1 or v2 tables; v3 tables start empty and first re-extraction populates them.
claims.rationale: Additive migration preserves existing data.
claims.excerpt: Schema migration v3 is additive — no touches to v1 or v2 tables.

claims.claim: Staleness is advisory, not blocking; a stale atlas still serves queries.
claims.rationale: Teams have legitimate reasons to run a slightly-stale atlas; staleness should respect those cases.
claims.excerpt: **Staleness is advisory, not blocking.** A stale atlas still serves queries.

claims.claim: Storage round-trip is lossless per ADR-06: atlas.json → SQLite → atlas.json produces a byte-identical file.
claims.rationale: Lossless round-trip is a storage discipline inherited from ADR-06.
claims.excerpt: Storage is lossless-round-trip per ADR-06: `atlas.json → SQLite → atlas.json` produces a byte-identical file.

claims.claim: `--check` CLI exits 0 when atlas matches HEAD, 1 when they differ, 2 when extracted_at_sha is absent or repo isn't a git tree; exit code is the whole contract.
claims.rationale: Stable exit-code contract avoids stdout parsing dependency.
claims.excerpt: The exit code is the whole contract — no dependency on stdout parsing.

claims.claim: `--check` does not start the MCP server or adapters; it is a cheap metadata read.
claims.rationale: Short-circuit mode minimizes overhead for CI/hooks.
claims.excerpt: `--check` does not start the MCP server or the adapters; it's a cheap metadata read.

claims.claim: atlas.json version bumps to "1.1" and adds git_commits and extracted_at_sha fields.
claims.rationale: Schema additions required to encode git data and staleness signal.
claims.excerpt: atlas.json additions (version bumps to `"1.1"`)

claims.claim: git_commits in atlas.json is sorted by date descending; files within each commit sorted ascending for deterministic diffs.
claims.rationale: Deterministic ordering keeps diffs reviewable.
claims.excerpt: Deterministic ordering keeps diffs reviewable.

claims.claim: impact_of_change uses file-level co-change, not commit-message semantic matching.
claims.rationale: Message-mining is a separate feature gated on future evidence.
claims.excerpt: `impact_of_change` uses file-level co-change, not "commits whose message mentions this symbol."

claims.claim: impact_of_change's compact IMPACT block format is load-bearing for step 11 tests; drift requires an ADR amendment.
claims.rationale: Tests depend on the exact format; changes need explicit ADR change.
claims.excerpt: The compact IMPACT block format above is load-bearing for step 11 tests; any drift requires an ADR amendment.

claims.claim: runExtractionPipeline gains a git phase between source indexing and claim writing; the phase is idempotent.
claims.rationale: Idempotency ensures byte-identical output on re-runs against unchanged state.
claims.excerpt: The phase is idempotent — running it on an up-to-date atlas re-walks the same 500 commits and produces byte-identical tables.

claims.claim: buildBundle picks up populated git block when the signal is in include; DEFAULT_SIGNALS adds "git".
claims.rationale: Bundle's return-everything-in-one-call philosophy now covers every declared axis.
claims.excerpt: `DEFAULT_SIGNALS` adds `"git"`

claims.claim: Storage layer accepts both v1.0 and v1.1 atlases; reading v1.0 still works but lacks git_commits/extracted_at_sha; every fresh extraction writes v1.1.
claims.rationale: Backward-compatible reads with forward-only writes.
claims.excerpt: The storage layer accepts both — reading a v1.0 atlas still works

claims.claim: get_symbol_context's git block shape matches the git field already declared in src/types.ts's SymbolContextBundle.
claims.rationale: Output rendering must align with the declared type.
claims.excerpt: Shape matches the `git` field already declared in `src/types.ts`'s `SymbolContextBundle`.

claims.claim: --budget-warn is advisory only: a single stderr warning fires when cumulative cost_usd exceeds threshold; the run continues and exit code is unaffected.
claims.rationale: Hard cap is a distinct feature not scoped for v0.2; semantic is intentionally loose.
claims.excerpt: This is advisory, not a hard cap: the run continues and the exit code is unaffected.

claims.claim: --check remains a flag (grandfathered) rather than a subcommand; future check-like probes will be subcommands, not flags.
claims.rationale: ADR-11 --check contract is external and one-way-migration-locked; asymmetry is bounded to this one case.
claims.excerpt: Flag-status is grandfathered for `--check`, not a pattern.

claims.claim: --full re-extracts every prose and docstring file (when stream runs); commits stay key-gated because they are immutable and re-billing filtered history needs its own explicit flag.
claims.rationale: L-7 decision for prompt/model changes; commit rebilling is a distinct feature.
claims.excerpt: Commits stay gated by their key: they are immutable, and `--full` exists for prompt or model changes

claims.claim: --json output emits a single JSON object on stdout with the same fields as key=value; new fields may appear, existing fields never rename; cost_usd is a number (not string) truncated to four decimals.
claims.rationale: Same stability contract; machine-consumable variant of the summary.
claims.excerpt: Same stability contract: new fields may appear, existing fields never rename.

claims.claim: --json prints exactly one JSON object on stdout; validate-extraction's result line is redirected to stderr under --json but stays on stdout under key=value.
claims.rationale: Preserves single-JSON-object stdout contract.
claims.excerpt: Under `--json` the validator's line now goes to stderr.

claims.claim: --verbose emits diagnostics to stderr; stdout stays pinned to the stable key=value or --json contract. --verbose and --json are orthogonal.
claims.rationale: Follows npm/git/curl convention; preserves stdout contract stability.
claims.excerpt: verbose amplifies the diagnostic channel, not the summary channel.

claims.claim: /index-atlas refresh writes symbols: [] on every refresh, runs resolve-symbols in Phase C step 1 before validate-extraction, and step 3 runs it again. Refresh carries baseline's extracted_at_sha and git_commits forward.
claims.rationale: F2 decision: atlas must not stay unloadable while extraction depth is fixed; git signal preservation prevents --check unknown-staleness reports.
claims.excerpt: **`symbols: []` on every refresh**

claims.claim: After an index that exports and exits 1, init should not be recommended (init skips extraction once atlas.json matches HEAD); instead recommend contextatlas index to retry.
claims.rationale: Prevents recovery-path dead-end where init hides failures.
claims.excerpt: `init` no longer says to re-run `init`, which skips extraction once `atlas.json` matches HEAD

claims.claim: Backward compatibility: --config-root, --config, and --check must behave exactly as before this ADR; any argv that worked against df39f7a must still work.
claims.rationale: Subcommand parsing is additive; existing contracts preserved.
claims.excerpt: Subcommand parsing is additive. Any argv that worked against `df39f7a` must still work

claims.claim: Canonical commit key is `commit:<sha>`; readers accept the legacy bare-sha form permanently; validate-atlas warns (exit 0) on bare-form keys and claim paths.
claims.rationale: F-5/L-2 canonicalization with permanent backward-read compatibility.
claims.excerpt: Every reader accepts the legacy bare-sha form permanently.

claims.claim: Commit stream is skipped (with info/warning) in non-git trees or when git unavailable; neither fails the run.
claims.rationale: Graceful degradation for non-git environments.
claims.excerpt: In a non-git tree, or when git is unavailable, the commit stream is skipped with an info log.

claims.claim: Docstring plan excludes files whose listSymbols failed and files that docs.include also matches (with one warning); commit plan is not capped (git signal keeps its 500-commit cap separately).
claims.rationale: Prevents replacing prose claims via same-relPath collision; enables full commit history extraction on first run.
claims.excerpt: both streams key by relPath, so extracting them here would replace their prose claims

claims.claim: Each subcommand defines its own 0/1/2 exit-code semantics; a unified scheme is rejected to preserve ADR-11's --check contract.
claims.rationale: Per-subcommand exit codes match POSIX conventions (git, npm, kubectl) and preserve external contracts.
claims.excerpt: Each subcommand defines its own 0/1/2 meanings

claims.claim: Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exits code 2 with an actionable error before any side-effect-bearing work; no .env file loading in v0.1.
claims.rationale: Fail fast with explicit guidance rather than cryptic SDK errors mid-run; keeps runtime deps minimal.
claims.excerpt: Not a cryptic SDK-level 401 surfaced after the pipeline has already started walking files. The check runs early, before any side-effect-bearing work.

claims.claim: New summary keys are appended after unverified_symbol_files in a fixed order; the 'new keys may be added, existing keys never renamed' rule holds. streams_enabled is comma-joined in key=value and an array in --json.
claims.rationale: Preserves output stability contract under three-stream widening.
claims.excerpt: Existing keys keep their names and order.

claims.claim: No adoption of commander, yargs, or oclif; hand-rolled parsing in cli-args.ts continues.
claims.rationale: Subcommand surface is small enough (v0.1: two; v0.5: maybe six) that a framework would be overkill.
claims.excerpt: No adoption of commander, yargs, or oclif. Hand-rolled parsing in `cli-args.ts` continues

claims.claim: No alias support: reindex, extract, refresh, build do not alias index. One canonical name per operation.
claims.rationale: Aliases proliferate and drift.
claims.excerpt: One canonical name per operation; aliases proliferate and drift.

claims.claim: No-subcommand invocation must remain MCP serving over stdio; this is a hard external contract to MCP clients and cannot be broken without a major version bump.
claims.rationale: Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and other MCP clients spawn the binary with no args expecting stdio JSON-RPC. One-way-migrations principle applies.
claims.excerpt: That is a hard external contract — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and any other compliant client depend on it.

claims.claim: One `index` command handles first-run, incremental, and --full paths transparently; no separate `contextatlas init` subcommand.
claims.rationale: 'Initialize' is not a distinct operation but the no-atlas-yet case of indexing.
claims.excerpt: One command, three paths. No separate `contextatlas init` subcommand

claims.claim: Output is always non-interactive: no terminal detection, progress bars, or colored output.
claims.rationale: The binary is scripted by both MCP clients and CI systems.
claims.excerpt: Output is always non-interactive.

claims.claim: README privacy note discloses that generate-adrs sends member names, docs.include globs matching source files send them whole, and the Skill does not extract docs.include pages.
claims.rationale: Privacy transparency about extraction data flows.
claims.excerpt: The README privacy note says that `generate-adrs` sends member names too

claims.claim: Subcommand detection is positional on the first user argument, inspected before flag parsing; flags may appear before or after the subcommand name.
claims.rationale: Enables flag position flexibility while keeping dispatch positional.
claims.excerpt: Subcommand is the first positional argument. Before any flag parsing, the parser inspects `argv[0]`

claims.claim: The operation is named 'index' rather than 'extract', 'reindex', 'refresh', or 'build' because it covers first-run and update cases uniformly and matches existing README documentation.
claims.rationale: Naming decision rationale; alternatives rejected for scope or presumption reasons.
claims.excerpt: `index` names the complete pipeline operation: walk, extract, resolve, store, export.

claims.claim: When a docstring or commit stream has any call attempted and all fail, the run finishes remaining streams and Stage 7, prints summary, writes stderr message, and exits 1. Only API/network errors count as failed; unparseable responses do not.
claims.rationale: Preserves paid work across streams; avoids blaming auth on parse errors.
claims.excerpt: Only calls that threw an API or network error (and, for commits, failed writes) count as failed

claims.claim: Zero-unresolved verbose case is silent; no stderr emission when every token resolves.
claims.rationale: Avoids noise without signal.
claims.excerpt: **Zero-unresolved case:** silent.

claims.claim: `index` accepts --config-root, --config, --full, --json, --budget-warn, --verbose; --check is rejected on `index` with an actionable error.
claims.rationale: Defines exact accepted flag surface for the subcommand.
claims.excerpt: `--check` — flag belongs to the no-subcommand mode (staleness probe); passing it alongside `index` is rejected with an actionable error

claims.claim: files_deleted counts prose deletions only; the F-4 bug had inflated it with docstring and commit keys.
claims.rationale: Restores documented meaning of the summary key.
claims.excerpt: `files_deleted` now counts prose deletions only

claims.claim: index must shut down adapter subprocesses cleanly on exit (success, failure, or signal); no zombie processes. Use finally-block shutdown discipline.
claims.rationale: Matches existing MCP-path discipline.
claims.excerpt: must shut them down cleanly on exit — success, failure, or signal. No zombie processes.

claims.claim: index never writes outside the configured atlas paths.
claims.rationale: Side-effect boundary constraint.
claims.excerpt: Never writes outside the configured atlas paths

claims.claim: index runs the pipeline in-process and exits; no long-running daemon mode.
claims.rationale: A daemon is a different product closer to a build server.
claims.excerpt: A long-running daemon that services extraction requests is a different product

claims.claim: manifest_version is '2' exactly when extraction.streams disables a stream, '1' otherwise; a pre-v1.2 /index-atlas Skill copy stops on any version but '1', preventing it from misreading a disabled-stream empty array as deleted sources.
claims.rationale: F3 fix: prior versioning let old Skills drop disabled-stream claims.
claims.excerpt: An `/index-atlas` copy from before v1.2 stops on any version but `"1"`

claims.claim: stdout key=value summary keys are stable: new keys may be added, existing keys are never renamed.
claims.rationale: One-way migrations principle applied to CI-consumable output.
claims.excerpt: `key=value` lines are stable across releases; new keys may be added, existing keys never renamed.

claims.claim: validate-atlas warns (exit 0, not error) when a claim's symbol_ids names an unlisted symbol, because this is the expected state of every /index-atlas refresh and emptying links loses them permanently.
claims.rationale: F2 rationale: warning-not-error preserves recovery paths.
claims.excerpt: It is a warning, not an error, because it is the expected state of every `/index-atlas` refresh

claims.claim: validate-extraction exempts docs-bucket pages, notes without ADR file names, and keys whose file is gone from adr_depth_floor and source_coverage; if the prose walk fails, nothing is exempt. It runs on every atlas.committed: true run with an atlas.json on disk, not only on runs that export.
claims.rationale: F1/F5 fixes: prevents exit-1 on docs pages under 8 claims; makes gate consistent across no-change runs.
claims.excerpt: `validate-extraction` checks only ADRs the current prose walk lists

claims.claim: A file whose getDocstring fails for any symbol is left out of the manifest entirely (mirrors CLI's all-or-nothing file rule); list-extraction-sources passes lsp.initialize_timeout_ms to its adapters.
claims.rationale: Prevents Skill refresh from dropping failed-symbol claims and pinning wrong SHA; unifies LSP timeout behavior.
claims.excerpt: the Skill keeps its claims and key

claims.claim: Stage 4a prunes stale symbols by ordered rules; a claim whose last link is removed becomes orphaned (kept in atlas, reported), never deleted by pruning.
claims.rationale: F-1 fix: stale symbols accumulated across runs; pruning must not silently delete claims.
claims.excerpt: Claims are never deleted by pruning. A claim whose last link is removed is **orphaned**

claims.claim: Subcommand dispatcher runs before loadConfig so different subcommands can have different config-error semantics.
claims.rationale: Loading config before knowing subcommand imposes one subcommand's error model on all.
claims.excerpt: **Dispatch before config load.** The subcommand dispatcher runs before `loadConfig`.

claims.claim: index extracts prose then docstring then commit in fixed order sharing one cost tracker; library runExtractionPipeline defaults to prose-only when deps.streams is omitted (pre-Phase-2 behavior).
claims.rationale: Prose-first ordering ensures early prose all-fail cannot discard later paid work; library default preserves backward compatibility.
claims.excerpt: Prose runs first so that its "every document failed" error... can never discard a later stream's paid work.

claims.claim: With atlas.committed: true, index checkpoints atlas.json during extraction (default 30s interval at unit boundaries) so an interrupted run keeps stored units; a checkpoint keeps the run-start extracted_at_sha (only Stage 7 stamps HEAD).
claims.rationale: Prevents re-billing paid work after interruption; preserves staleness semantics until final export.
claims.excerpt: a checkpoint keeps the `extracted_at_sha` the run started from

claims.claim: Docstring file writes are all-or-nothing per file in one transaction; a failing call leaves prior claims and key untouched and stops the file's remaining calls. Commit writes are per-commit transactions; unparseable commit responses are pinned with zero claims (not retried).
claims.rationale: L-10 write and failure semantics; commits are immutable so re-billing deterministic failures buys nothing.
claims.excerpt: Its claims are replaced and its SHA pinned only when every call for the file succeeded, in one transaction

claims.claim: Cost preview is printed to stderr only when the plan has at least one model call; not interactive, no confirmation; stdout stays a single JSON object under --json.
claims.rationale: Preserves stdout contract; --budget-warn remains the in-run guard.
claims.excerpt: Before the first model call, `index` prints an estimate to **stderr**. stdout is unchanged

claims.claim: Flags are orthogonal modifiers that compose across operations; subcommands partition distinct operations with distinct arg shapes, outputs, stdio contracts, and exit-code semantics.
claims.rationale: This is the governing architectural rule for every CLI addition from v0.1 forward.
claims.excerpt: Flags are orthogonal modifiers that work across operations... Subcommands are distinct operations with distinct argument shapes, distinct outputs, distinct stdio contracts, and distinct exit-code semantics.

claims.claim: Source keys are classified as prose, docstring, or commit primarily by claim source prefix; zero-claim keys use shape fallback in a fixed order. Language-extension registry is typed such that adding a language without an entry fails compilation.
claims.rationale: Stream-aware classification prevents F-4 mass-deletion; type-enforced registry prevents drift.
claims.excerpt: adding a language without an entry fails compilation

claims.claim: Stage 0.5 migrates bare 40-hex commit keys to canonical `commit:<sha>` form; runs on every index, is idempotent, and counts as a modification for Stage 7.
claims.rationale: F-5 fix: two paths wrote two forms; canonical form is the standard going forward. Installed Skills are never overwritten so migration must be permanent.
claims.excerpt: `commit:<sha>` is the `source_shas` key and the `claims.source_path` of every commit claim

claims.claim: Skill-path resolve-symbols applies the same prune rules as CLI; drops symbol_ids entries with no matching symbol; reports orphaned claims.
claims.rationale: Prevents dangling FK ids that made importer reject atlas; parity between CLI and Skill paths.
claims.excerpt: `claims[].symbol_ids` entries with no matching symbol are dropped

claims.claim: atlas.json is written atomically: to <atlas>.tmp then renamed. On Windows EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, retry 4 times 50ms apart then fall back to direct write (not atomic). Symlink targets are preserved.
claims.rationale: Readers and interrupted writes see old or new file; Windows-specific handling documented.
claims.excerpt: it writes `<atlas>.tmp`, then renames it over `atlas.json`, so a reader or a kill sees the old file or the new one

claims.claim: MCP server logs one startup warning when serving a non-empty cache and atlas.json's generated_at differs from the cache's atlas_meta generated_at; remedy is to stop server, delete local cache, restart. resolve-symbols keeps generated_at so standalone runs don't trigger the warning.
claims.rationale: Server does not re-import (Phase 4); warning surfaces stale-cache state.
claims.excerpt: it logs one warning at startup that names the remedy

claims.claim: A torn or conflicted atlas.json fails to import with a message naming the file and the git checkout remedy; claim links to unlisted symbols fail with a message naming affected claim count and pointing to resolve-symbols.
claims.rationale: Actionable errors rather than bare SyntaxError or FK constraint failures.
claims.excerpt: not a bare `SyntaxError`

claims.claim: index, MCP server, and init smoke test import atlas.json only into an empty cache (no symbols, claims, or source keys); with atlas.committed: false the cache is source of truth and atlas.json only seeds an empty cache.
claims.rationale: F6 fix: prevents leftover atlas.json from replacing cache work on every server start.
claims.excerpt: The cache is now the source of truth: `atlas.json` only seeds an empty cache and is otherwise not read

claims.claim: A local cache with a schema version above the latest this build knows is used as-is with a warning; a later release would skip its own migrations up to that version.
claims.rationale: Schema guard for forward-compatibility when caches are shared across builds.
claims.excerpt: A local cache whose schema version is above the latest this build knows... is used as it is, with a warning

claims.claim: Stage 5 applies per-stream deletion rules: prose deleted iff absent from prose walk (including under --full), docstring deleted iff file missing (or under configured adapter exclude when stream runs), commit never deleted.
claims.rationale: F-4 fix: prior key-based deletion mass-deleted docstring/commit streams; commit retention preserves ADR-11 v0.8 LOCK 2.b.
claims.excerpt: commit | never (the v0.8 LOCK 2.b retain discipline, which the key-based delete had silently broken)

claims.claim: symbol_candidates is stored in the local cache and preserved by importer/exporter (emitted after symbol_ids when non-empty); it never reaches Claim or MCP tool output; atlas schema stays 1.4.
claims.rationale: F-7 fix: field survives CLI runs without changing MCP output.
claims.excerpt: The field never reaches `Claim` or MCP tool output; that output is byte-identical.

claims.claim: Per-call diagnostic readiness uses waitForDiagnostics helper with 1000ms ceiling; Pyright emits no $/progress so cold-start absorbs into the per-call ceiling (pyright-fallback path of ADR-18)
claims.rationale: Describes how diagnostic readiness is handled given Pyright's lack of progress notifications
claims.excerpt: Per-call diagnostic-readiness uses the `waitForDiagnostics` helper (1000ms ceiling). Pyright emits no `$/progress` for analysis-completion

claims.claim: Full indexing uses two passes (pass-1 computes isProtocol cache, pass-2 computes extends/implements/usedByTypes); single-symbol operations stay single-pass; only getTypeInfo needs the cache
claims.rationale: Keeps query latency proportional to single-symbol work, not repo size
claims.excerpt: **Single-symbol operations (`listSymbols`, `getSymbolDetails`, `findReferences`, `getDiagnostics`) stay single-pass.** These return file-local data and don't need inventory-wide Protocol awareness. Only `getTypeInfo` needs the cache.

claims.claim: When Protocol cache unavailable at query time, adapter falls back to mechanisms (a)+(b) only; project-defined Protocols route to `extends` until cache is built — degraded but not incorrect (less-lossy error direction)
claims.rationale: Acceptable degradation: leaving a Protocol in extends is the less-lossy error than the opposite
claims.excerpt: This is a degraded mode but not incorrect — the ADR-07 contract says `implements` contains Protocols; failing to detect a project-defined Protocol means leaving it in `extends`, which is the less-lossy error direction.

claims.claim: jedi-language-server / pylsp rejected because they cannot satisfy ADR-07's getTypeInfo contract (no reliable cross-file type inference, no inverse-lookup)
claims.rationale: Capability disqualifier for the load-bearing getTypeInfo contract
claims.excerpt: Rejected as a hard disqualifier: lacks reliable type-inference for `textDocument/references` across files, and has no inverse-lookup story for type relationships.
